confidence_evidence.interpretation: Evidence aggregation score for review prioritization; not a calibrated probability.

quality_gates.rationale: A page-level mean below 0.90 warrants review, while structural checks decide whether extraction must stop.
The lower-confidence tail is monitored independently so a high mean cannot hide weak tokens.
Every configured summary table must expose all reporting periods before financial cells can be interpreted safely.
At least 90 percent of financial rows should retain labels; unlabeled values remain inspectable rather than guessed.
Period-column mistakes directly change financial meaning and therefore require near-complete assignment.
A weak note location can route every later stage to unrelated pages.
Sparse OCR damage may be retained with warnings, but broad column-assignment failure requires review.
At least 80 percent of visibly numeric note cells should parse; lower rates trigger explicit partial-quality status.
A required relation cannot be successful while a reporting period remains financially unexplained.
This is an exploratory manual-review threshold, not a statistically calibrated probability cutoff.
Missing pages, periods, notes, tables, or referenced rows invalidate the output structure.
Invalid confidence, bounding-box, or normalized-value representations violate the output contract.
An applicable exact financial reconciliation must not disagree silently.
OCR-damaged inputs may prevent a reconciliation; incompleteness remains visible without inventing values.
Warnings from extraction and model stages must propagate into the validation status.

structural.message: Configured summary pages must be represented by structured tables.
Every summary table must expose the document reporting periods exactly once.
Every configured note must exist and contain at least one structured table.
Relation identifiers must resolve to emitted summary and note rows.

format.message: Every confidence must be finite and in [0, 1].
Every bounding box must contain non-negative integer geometry.
Numeric status and normalized value must remain semantically coherent.

financial.message: Total assets must equal total liabilities and equity for every reporting period.
Every emitted summary subtotal and total should carry exact, non-overlapping reconciliation evidence.
Ambiguous OCR normalizations must remain reviewable and any selected correction must have exact financial evidence.
The first total row must equal the exact sum of preceding detail rows.

limitations: Quality thresholds are transparent engineering thresholds, not statistically calibrated probabilities.
The reviewed relation set contains only two examples, so confidence is intended for evidence aggregation and review prioritization.
Incomplete financial checks preserve OCR uncertainty instead of substituting expected values.
